name: Google News
description: Google News is Google's personalized news discovery and aggregation product, with separate publisher eligibility, crawl, Search Console performance, Showcase, and reader-revenue surfaces.
agentUseSummary: Google News is not available through Relay. Google publishes no supported API for third parties to retrieve or automate a user's Google News feed, topics, saved stories, followed sources, alerts, or search results. Publisher Center and Search Console APIs serve publishers' own publication and performance workflows, not news-content retrieval. Relay will use licensed publisher or news-provider APIs instead of scraping Google News.

blocked.label: Connect Google News
blocked.description: Google publishes no supported delegated API for a reader's Google News content, personalization, library, follows, or settings.

blocked.label: Read Google News feeds or search
blocked.description: Personalized feeds, topics, local news, searches, rankings, recommendations, snippets, full coverage, and source groupings remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Change reader state
blocked.description: Following topics or sources, saving stories, hiding sources, changing language or location, managing alerts, and modifying personalization are blocked.

blocked.label: Manage publications
blocked.description: Publication, organization, Showcase, reader-revenue, user-permission, policy, sitemap, and Search Console changes are outside this reader provider and remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use private or scraped News interfaces
blocked.description: Undocumented RSS URLs, private endpoints, scraping, browser automation, cookie or session capture, result republishing, and article-text extraction from Google News are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unsupported
approvalProfiles.description: No Google News action is enabled because Google publishes no delegated reader API; news research must use licensed sources with their own provenance and usage contracts.

runtimeSupport.description: No Google News wrapper is mounted without a published reader API and content-licensing contract.

providerSetup.blocker: Google's current News documentation describes first-party personalized reader features and publisher-facing crawl, policy, Search Console, Showcase and revenue workflows. It does not publish a developer endpoint, delegated reader OAuth scope, token lifecycle, quota, webhook or content-license contract for retrieving a user's feed, following state, saved stories, alerts or Google News searches. Publisher Center is not a CMS or content API, and since March 2025 Google automatically generates publication pages and no longer uses RSS feeds or web locations submitted there. Search Console's googleNews search type returns a verified publisher site's own performance analytics, not reader content or search results.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep Google News unavailable. For news research, integrate a provider that explicitly licenses discovery metadata and article access, or use publisher-owned RSS and APIs under each source's terms, preserving source, author, publication time, canonical URL, paywall, update and correction metadata. Product owners may link users to Google News in their browser, but Relay must not capture sessions, scrape results, depend on undocumented Google News RSS endpoints, reproduce publisher text, or modify publisher or reader settings. Reconsider only if Google publishes a supported delegated reader API and content-use contract.

evidence.supports: Google defines Publisher Center as a publisher settings, News Showcase and reader-revenue surface, explicitly not an authoring tool or CMS, and says web content is automatically considered for News.
Google states that News fully transitioned to automatically generated publication pages in March 2025 and no longer uses publisher-submitted RSS feeds or web locations for those pages.
Google's documented googleNews API type is part of Search Console Search Analytics for a publisher's own performance reports, not a Google News feed or content-search API.
Google describes Google News ranking and personalization as first-party algorithmic behavior based on relevance, authority, freshness, usability, location, language and user interests.
Google applies news-specific content, transparency, sponsorship and misleading-content policies to publisher eligibility and may remove violating sources from News surfaces.
